title: FCW with AEB cut front-to-rear crashes 49%; AEB cut pickup rear-end crash rates 43% (November 2022)
summary: VOA Learning English (16 Nov 2022): the automaker-NHTSA Partnership for Analytics Research in Traffic Safety analyzed 12 million police-reported crashes in 13 states; IIHS analyzed pickups in 25 st...
account: VOA Learning English reported on 16 Nov 2022, drawing on Associated Press coverage, that two U.S. studies had quantified the effect of front crash prevention. The Partnership for Analytics Research in Traffic Safety, a collaboration between automakers and the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, examined more than 12 million police-reported crashes in 13 states involving 93 vehicle models from 2015 to 2020 and found front-to-rear crashes reduced by 49% when the striking vehicle had both forward collision warning and automatic emergency braking, with injury crashes down 53%; Stellantis executive Tim Czapp of the PARTS board was quoted. The Insurance Institute for Highway Safety, using police-reported crashes in 25 states from 2017 to 2020, found automatic emergency braking reduced rear-end crash rates for pickups by 43%; IIHS researcher Jessica Cicchino urged automakers to fit every pickup with the feature. The PARTS and IIHS reports themselves were not read (an IIHS page guess returned 404); the OECD AI Incidents Monitor lists the coverage (2022-11-15-d32d) as an aggregate benefit. These are different studies from the 2017 IIHS analysis already in the database as AIBD-0008. The date given is the publication date.
purpose: Forward collision warning and automatic emergency braking are built to detect an impending front-to-rear collision and warn or brake.
system: Forward collision warning and automatic emergency braking across multiple makers' passenger vehicles and pickups

ratings.reason: Aggregate crash-rate findings; no individually attributable outcome.

ai_role.statement: Camera and radar perception triggers warnings and braking; the studies compare crash rates of equipped and unequipped vehicles using police-reported crash data, and the underlying reports were not read.

evidence.title: Study: Vehicle Warning and Braking Systems Cut Crashes by 50 Percent
evidence.quote: Front to rear crashes were reduced by 49 percent when the striking vehicle had both forward collision warning and automatic emergency braking.

evidence.title: Automatic Emergency Braking AI Significantly Reduces Vehicle Crashes
evidence.quote: Two U.S. studies found that automatic emergency braking, an AI system that detects imminent collisions and applies brakes, can halve rear-end crashes and reduce pickup truck crashes by over 40%.

echoes.setting: IIHS 2017 analysis of FCW and AEB on rear-end striking crash rates (already in the database as AIBD-0008)

headline: FCW with AEB cuts front-to-rear crashes 49%

comparator.against: striking vehicles without forward collision warning and automatic emergency braking
comparator.after: front to rear crashes were reduced by 49 percent
comparator.quote: The PARTS group’s study found that front to rear crashes were reduced by 49 percent when the striking vehicle had both forward collision warning and automatic emergency braking.

later.note: PARTS's second study, published 6 January 2025 on model years 2015-2023, again measured a 49% reduction in front-to-rear crashes for AEB-equipped vehicles, with effectiveness rising from 46% for 2015-2017 models to 52% for 2021-2023 models; NHTSA had meanwhile finalized a rule in April 2024 requiring AEB on all new light vehicles by September 2029.
later.quote: The study measured a 49% reduction in front-to-rear crashes for vehicles equipped with AEB across all vehicle segments and model years.
